You'll research and experiment with prompting techniques and applied AI methods, author the exemplar use cases the rest of the function copies, and teach what you learn: delivering technical onboarding for new Legal Engineers in your region and broadcasting best practices to the team worldwide. And because judgement needs grounding, around 30% of your time stays on live client work, chosen for what it teaches.
 Specifically, you will 
 • Vet the Skills Library and Legal Engineering outputs against the quality bar: review skills, workflows and use cases hands-on before they go live, and quality-control practice-area workflows for consistency.
 • Research and experiment with prompting techniques, skill patterns and emerging AI methods, and turn what works into best practices the whole function adopts.
 • Author the reference use cases that show what great looks like, published as the exemplars others copy.
 • Work closely with the Product team on up-and-coming capabilities: early hands-on testing, the first best practices for new features, and structured feedback from real use.
 • Produce materials that would support the technical onboarding and training for new Legal Engineers in your region, such as best practices to create use cases etc.
 • Communicate new best practices, exemplars and platform changes to the Legal Engineering team worldwide.
 • Support the flagship demos our CEO and C-suite take on stage at the industry’s biggest events: use case preparation, fixtures and rehearsal support.
 • Oversee the quality and currency of the use case and skills libraries, including coordination across regions
 • Spend roughly 30% of your time on live client work, selected for what it feeds back into the standards and libraries.
 What you bring 
 You're a lawyer with real practice experience who has become genuinely technical: maybe you did a coding bootcamp, maybe you taught yourself, but either way you're the person colleagues ask how something actually works. You live in AI tools, and it shows: you can tell a strong use case from a plausible-sounding weak one, you know why a prompt underperforms before you've finished reading it, and you hold both halves of the judgement this role needs: what makes a prompt run well, and what makes a legal output substantively right rather than merely fluent. When you vet, you vet properly: line by line against the source, with the discipline to put the AI down when the job calls for your own eyes.
 We're looking for 
 • A qualified lawyer with solid practice experience at a leading firm or in-house team, or equivalent: enough substantive judgement to vet outputs across practice areas.
 • Real technical prowess: comfortable with code or scripting (a bootcamp or self-taught background counts entirely), and fluent in the mechanics of how AI tools actually behave.
 • A heavy, habitual user of AI, ideally legal AI, with sharp prompt and use case discernment: able to rank a strong prompt against a mediocre one, articulate exactly why, and improve it.
 • Visible pride in the craft of prompting and use case design: someone who wants to be the reference point for what good looks like.
 • Rigour in review: line-by-line verification against source, and the judgement to know exactly when not to use AI.
 • Comfortable running high-throughput workstreams: you triage well, keep many threads moving, and build process where volume demands it.
 • Experience building skills, workflows or automations in a legal AI platform is a strong plus.
 • Good to have: an M&A or wider transactional background, or deal coordination experience.
 Where this role can go 
 This role is built to grow with the field itself. Applied legal AI knowledge barely exists as a discipline yet, and nobody accumulates evidence faster than the person vetting and testing the entire output of a global function. Do this job well and you are positioned to become one of the industry’s recognised voices on what good looks like. Inside Legora, the role is designed to grow into owning applied AI knowledge globally: the standards, techniques and systems every region operates on. Growth is subject to performance and company need, but the direction is deliberate: master the material here first, then define the standard for the industry.

items.jobDescription:
About Allica Bank 
 Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.
 Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.
 Department Description 
 Security is a hands-on, delivery-focused team that helps Allica Bank move quickly while maintaining strong, proportionate, and effective security controls.
 The team combines day-to-day operational support with continuous improvement, automation, control assurance, and stakeholder partnership across the bank.
 We work closely with Technology, Engineering, Product and business teams to make security practical and effective, while ensuring our controls support the requirements of a regulated banking environment.
 Role Description 
 The purpose of this role is to strengthen Allica Bank's identity and access controls by making access easier to request, safer to approve and simpler to evidence. The role will combine day-to-day IAM operations with engineering, automation, and continuous improvement to reduce manual effort and improve the security and governance of identity services.
 The role sits within Security and focuses on Identity and Access Management, primarily across Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Entra Identity Governance, Azure identity, access management and security controls, with support for Google Cloud Platform IAM governance, engineering and automation as that capability develops.
 The successful candidate will contribute to the day-to-day running of IAM services, including access requests, joiner/mover/leaver activity, access reviews, privileged access, RBAC, application SSO, and application onboarding. Alongside BAU responsibilities, they will identify and deliver improvements to processes, controls, and automation.
 This is not a purely operational IAM role. The successful candidate will be expected to run IAM services, engineer improvements, automate repeatable work, strengthen controls and help mature identity services across the bank.
 Experience using automation and AI tools to improve processes, reduce manual effort and strengthen security controls is desirable.
 Success in this role will be measured through the quality and timeliness of IAM operations, stronger identity governance and evidence, improved automation, and reduced manual effort.
 Principal Accountabilities 
 Operate and maintain IAM services, including user lifecycle management, access requests, provisioning, deprovisioning and access changes across Microsoft Entra ID and integrated applications.
 Manage identity governance and access controls, including Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), least-privilege access, Conditional Access and Privileged Identity Management (PIM).
 Manage access reviews and certifications, including reviewer engagement, evidence collection, exception handling, remediation tracking and reporting.
 Onboard and integrate applications into the IAM/IGA platform, including SSO, SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning and secure authentication using Microsoft Entra ID.
 Support application and vendor onboarding from an IAM perspective, assessing authentication, provisioning, privileged access, logging, ownership and access review requirements.
 Maintain effective IAM controls and audit evidence, supporting internal and external audits and regulatory requirements.
 Identify and deliver improvements through automation, improved workflows, better request processes, clearer ownership and enhanced reporting, reducing manual effort and improving control effectiveness.
 Support identity-related issues and investigations, working with application owners, Technology, Security and other stakeholders to resolve access issues and manage associated risks.
 Maintain IAM documentation and operational standards, including process guides, access models, onboarding standards, control evidence, and runbooks.
 Support wider identity and cloud access services where needed, including Azure identity, access management and security controls, credential lifecycle management, and Google Cloud IAM governance, engineering and automation.
 Provide clear reporting to Security leadership, highlighting IAM risks, control status, work in progress, blockers, and remediation actions.
 Support related control and regulatory activities, including Risk Smart Indicators and Data Subject Access Requests, where IAM input or evidence is needed.
 Personal Attributes & Experience 
 Experience in Identity and Access Management, Security Operations, Cloud Security or technical operations, ideally within a regulated or control-focused environment.
 Good hands-on knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID and Azure identity, access management and security controls, including users, groups, Enterprise Applications, SSO, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management and access management controls.
 Understanding of IAM principles and controls, including least privilege, RBAC, privileged access, joiner/mover/leaver processes and segregation of duties.
 Experience supporting access reviews, remediation, audit evidence and operational controls, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
 Comfortably balancing BAU operational work with hands-on engineering, including improving processes, writing or adapting scripts, documenting workflows and automating repeatable tasks.
 Able to work effectively with application owners, Technology, Security, suppliers and non-technical stakeholders to translate access requirements into practical and secure controls.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate access issues, identify root causes, and recommend practical improvements.
 Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain identity risks, controls and needed actions in plain English.
 Strong ownership and accountability, particularly where access approvals, evidence, remediation and control outcomes are involved.
 Understands the importance of effective, auditable controls in an FCA/PRA-regulated environment.
 Able to consider the end-user experience when designing and improving access processes, balancing security, usability, and operational efficiency.
 Microsoft identity and governance: Microsoft Entra Identity Governance, Conditional Access, PIM, access reviews and Enterprise Applications
 Automation and scripting: Microsoft Graph, PowerShell, Logic Apps, Azure Functions or similar automation tooling
 Azure identity, access management and security controls
 Application integration: SAML, SCIM, OAuth, OpenID Connect, SSO onboarding and secure provisioning patterns
 Google Cloud Platform IAM governance, access models, engineering standards and automation
 1Password or similar credential management platforms
 Cloud audit logging and identity monitoring
 Service desk and IT workflow platforms
 The successful candidate does not need experience across every technology listed. Curiosity, the ability to learn quickly, and a strong understanding of IAM principles are more important than knowledge of a specific product.
 Working at Allica Bank 
 At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.
 Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:
 Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities
 Options for flexible working
 Regular social activities
 Pension contributions
 Discretionary bonus scheme
 Private health cover
 Life assurance
 Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave
 Don’t tick every box? 
 Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!
 Flexible working 
 We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.
 Diversity 
 We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

Wordsmith 
 Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.
 We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.
 Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.
 We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.
 More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com , Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI .
 The role 
 Deployment Engineers own the technical side of getting Wordsmith live inside a customer.
 Once a deal is signed, you’ll connect Wordsmith to the systems our customers already run on. That means identity and SSO, Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management, chat tools, and MCP connections to the wider AI and data stack. You’ll design how data and permissions flow between them, build and test the integrations, and work through each customer’s IT and security requirements until everything works in production.
 It’s part integration engineering, part solutions architecture, and part customer-facing problem solving. You’ll be the technical lead on every deployment you own, the person customer IT teams talk to, and the person who works out how to make it work when an integration doesn’t behave as documented.
 This is a technical, hands-on role. You don’t need to be a lawyer, and we’re not necessarily looking for one. We’re looking for engineers and technical consultants who understand identity, APIs and enterprise SaaS, and who enjoy making systems talk to each other. Your focus is the technical foundation the rest of the deployment runs on.
 You’ll work side by side with our Legal Engineers on every deployment. While you connect Wordsmith to the customer’s systems, they configure the platform itself: workflows, agents, playbooks and automations built around how the legal team works. You’ll plan the deployment together, agree what each integration needs to support, and make sure the connections you build give their configuration the data, documents and permissions it depends on.
 What you’ll do 
 1. Integrations 
 Own the integrations for each deployment, including SSO and SCIM, Microsoft 365, SharePoint and OneDrive, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management and chat tools
 Configure and connect Wordsmith to customers’ wider AI and data stack through MCP
 Build, test and harden integrations so they hold up in production, not just in a demo
 2. Identity, Security & Access 
 Set up identity and access, including SSO with Okta, Entra ID and Google, user provisioning, roles and permissions
 Work through customers’ security reviews, IT questionnaires and data-handling requirements
 Make sure permissions in Wordsmith respect the permissions in the systems it connects to
 3. Technical Solution Design 
 Take the technical handover from Sales and confirm the customer’s systems landscape, constraints and integration scope
 Design how data, documents and requests flow between Wordsmith and the customer’s tools
 Advise customer IT on the right architecture for their environment and where the trade-offs sit
 Work with Legal Engineers to agree what each integration needs to support the workflows, agents and playbooks they’re configuring
 4. Technical Delivery & Escalation 
 Lead the technical workstream of each deployment, from environment setup and integration build through testing to go-live
 Diagnose and fix integration issues, and act as the escalation point for technical problems during rollout
 Know when a problem needs Engineering, and bring them a clear, reproducible case
 5. Improve How We Integrate 
 Turn what you learn into reusable integration patterns, setup guides and technical runbooks
 Feed connector gaps, API limitations and recurring requests back to Product and Engineering
 What we’re looking for 
 Hands-on experience deploying and integrating enterprise SaaS in customer environments
 Strong working knowledge of identity and access, including SSO (SAML, OIDC), SCIM provisioning, Okta, Entra ID or Google Workspace
 Experience integrating with the Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace or Salesforce ecosystems
 Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, authentication flows and reading technical documentation. You can script or write code where it helps
 Familiarity with MCP or other ways of connecting AI systems to tools and data, or a strong appetite to learn
 Credible with customer IT and security teams. You can answer their questions and stand behind your architecture
 Methodical troubleshooter who isolates problems, reproduces them and fixes them
 Clear communicator who can explain a technical decision to a non-technical stakeholder
 Typical backgrounds include 
 Deployment, integration or implementation engineers in SaaS
 Solutions engineers or solutions architects
 Technical consultants with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or Salesforce experience
 IT or identity engineers who have moved into customer-facing roles
 How we work 
 We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.
 We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you’ll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.
 You’ll sit in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP of Transformation, and work closely with our Legal Engineers, alongside Legal Intelligence, Enablement, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product.
 Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation, and Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability.
 Why Wordsmith 
 Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding within larger organisations. Wordsmith is only as useful as the systems it connects to. Every new customer brings a different stack, and Deployment Engineers are the people who make Wordsmith work inside it.
 You’ll work directly with ambitious in-house legal teams, see how dozens of legal functions really operate, and take that back into a product you help shape. You will work across enterprise identity, productivity and CRM platforms, and on MCP as it develops into a standard. You will own real technical outcomes from your first week and help define how we integrate as we scale.

items.jobDescription:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . 
 We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
 You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
 This is a remote opportunity and we are looking for candidates from the UK, Sweden, Spain or Germany.
 About the role: 
 Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.
 The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.
 What You’ll Do 
 Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
 Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
 Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
 Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
 Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
 Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
 Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
 Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
 We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)
 On-Call 
 Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.
 What We’re Looking For: 
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
 Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
 Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
 Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
 Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
 Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
 Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
 Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.
 Nice to Have: 
 Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
 Open-source contributions.
 Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.
 In the UK, the Base compensation range for this role is £103,958 - £124,750.  Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable) and other benefits listed here . #LI-Remote 
 #LI-Remote 
 *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. 
 Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 
 100% Remote, Global Culture -  As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
 Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
 Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
 Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
 Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
 Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
 Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
 Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
 Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
 In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. 
 Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. 
 Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

 Summary
 Dust is hiring a User Researcher to be the connective tissue between our users and the teams building for them. This is a high-leverage, embedded research role — your work will directly shape product decisions, inform GTM positioning, and surface the insights that help us serve customers like Datadog, 1Password, and Cursor at a higher level. You'll be the first dedicated researcher on the team, which means you'll build the function from the ground up, sitting close to the people shipping the product every day.
 What you'll do
 Build and own the research function 
 Define the research practice at Dust: methodologies, tooling, cadences, and documentation standards
 Establish a consistent feedback loop between qualitative insights and product and GTM decisions
 Create reusable research assets and templates the whole team can leverage
 Run end-to-end research studies 
 Design and execute qualitative and quantitative studies — interviews, usability tests, concept tests, and surveys
 Identify the highest-leverage research questions and prioritise ruthlessly against the roadmap
 Deliver findings in formats that drive action, not just documentation
 Partner with Product and Design 
 Embed into product and design workflows so research informs decisions before they're made, not after
 Participate in roadmap discussions as a consistent, evidence-based voice for the user
 Challenge assumptions with data when it matters — and when it's uncomfortable
 Support GTM and customer understanding 
 Partner with Sales and Customer Success to surface patterns across customer conversations
 Help position Dust's value more precisely by understanding how users actually describe their problems and outcomes
 Contribute to ICP definition and segmentation work grounded in primary research
 Scale your impact with AI 
 Integrate AI-assisted research tools into your practice to move faster and cover more ground
 Build systems that allow the team to self-serve research insights without requiring your direct involvement every time
 Requirements
 Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions. Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.
 Aptitude 
 Strong mixed-methods research skills — you know when to go qualitative, when to go quantitative, and how to triangulate both into a clear point of view
 Experience running and synthesising user interviews at pace without sacrificing rigour or clarity
 Ability to translate complex user insights into decision-driving narratives that land with engineers, PMs, and founders alike
 Track record of research directly influencing product or business decisions — not just documentation that gets filed and forgotten
 Actively integrates AI tools to increase research velocity and coverage, treating it as a core part of how you work
 Attitude 
 Genuinely user-obsessed — you bring the user into conversations that aren't explicitly about research

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.




MISSION



We are developing, manufacturing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable spacecraft which will carry cargo to space stations and potentially humans in the longer run.



We are seeking an experienced Certification Engineer to join our Thermal Control System & Environmental Control and Life Support System team. You will be responsible for leading, coordinating, and driving the certification and verification closure activities of the Nyx Thermal Control System (TCS) and Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) in support of vehicle qualification, NASA certification, and flight acceptance.



The role serves as the primary focal point between the TCS & ECLSS teams, System Engineering, Verification & Validation, Chief Engineering Office, AIT, Program, Safety Engineering, and external stakeholders. The Certification Engineer ensures that TCS and ECLSS requirements are properly allocated, verified, traceable, and closed with appropriate evidence, while maintaining alignment with NASA SSP requirements, Data Item Deliverables (DIDs), verification plans, and Safety Review Panel expectations.



The position requires a strong understanding of spacecraft systems engineering, thermal engineering, verification methodologies, qualification logic, and agency review processes to ensure that technical evidence across both subsystems is complete, credible, traceable, and accepted by the certification authorities.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




LEAD THERMAL & ECLSS VERIFICATION CLOSURE ACTIVITIES

 - Own the verification closure process for TCS and ECLSS, from subsystem level through spacecraft-level qualification.

 - Ensure TCS and ECLSS requirements are allocated to appropriate verification methods.

 - Coordinate the preparation, execution, and closure of verification events with analysts, product owners, subsystem engineers, system engineers, and test teams.

 - Maintain consistency between the TCS & ECLSS verification strategies and spacecraft-level verification planning.

 - Ensure analyses, test reports, inspection records, NCRs, requirement justifications, and review documentation are available to support certification closure.

 - Support the preparation of qualification, certification, and flight readiness reviews.

 - Ensure consistency of verification logic and evidence across TCS and ECLSS, particularly for requirements, interfaces, functions, or verification activities involving both subsystems.


MANAGE NASA REQUIREMENT COMPLIANCE AND VERIFICATION PRODUCT

 - Act as the TCS & ECLSS focal point for NASA certification and verification activities.

 - Coordinate the closure of applicable NASA SSP requirements and associated verification products, including the DIDs.

 - Ensure consistency between analyses, test results, requirements, qualification rationale, and certification documentation across both subsystems.

 - Maintain alignment between NASA verification expectations and TEC verification approaches.

 - Coordinate with TCS and ECLSS technical owners to ensure certification evidence is technically robust and delivered according to program and customer milestones.


LEAD THERMAL & ECLSS CONTRIBUTIONS TO SAFETY REVIEWS

 - Prepare and coordinate TCS & ECLSS contributions to NASA Safety Reviews.

 - Ensure TCS and ECLSS hazards, controls, verification evidence, and closure rationale are fully documented.

 - Support and coordinate the development of safety review presentations and supporting technical packages.

 - Ensure consistency between hazard reports, verification evidence, and qualification activities.

 - Coordinate with Safety Engineering and subsystem technical owners to ensure certification evidence supporting hazard-control verification is identified and available.


SUPPORT QUALIFICATION AND TEST CAMPAIGNS

 - Ensure qualification, acceptance, development, and integrated test campaigns provide the evidence required for certification.

 - Identify verification gaps early and drive mitigation actions.

 - Support preparation of verification plans, qualification matrices, and closure notices.

 - Participate in major test reviews and assess certification impacts of anomalies and non-conformances.

 - Support requirement closure from TVAC, Thermal Balance, functional testing, and integrated spacecraft verification campaigns.

 - Drive the closure of actions and verification-related NCRs

 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS




TECHNICAL

 - MSc or equivalent degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.

 - Strong understanding of spacecraft thermal control system, ECLSS, and spacecraft development processes.

 - Experience with spacecraft verification and qualification methodologies.

 - Familiarity with NASA and/or ECSS verification standards, requirements management, verification matrices, and closure processes.

 - Understanding of thermal analyses, thermal testing, qualification logic, and evidence generation.


EXPERIENCE

 - 8+ years of experience in spacecraft development, system engineering, verification, certification, or thermal engineering.

 - Experience supporting spacecraft design reviews and qualification campaigns.

 - Experience interfacing with external customers, agencies, or certification authorities.

 - Experience managing complex technical documentation and evidence packages.


PERSONAL SKILLS

 - Strong organization, coordination, technical writing, and communication skills.

 - Ability to drive closure of multidisciplinary actions across engineering teams.

 - High level of rigor, traceability, and attention to detail.

 - Ability to challenge assumptions and ensure certification readiness.

 - Comfort presenting technical material to senior engineering leadership and external review boards.
   
   

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

 - We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

 - We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

 - We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. 
 
The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We Are Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 
 You Are 
 You are a front-end engineer who actually understands DFT, not just at the handoff level, but deep enough to know why a scan chain fails, why a compression ratio tanks, or why an ATPG tool chokes on certain RTL constructs. Most front-end engineers treat DFT as someone else's problem. You learned early that this creates expensive problems downstream, so you made it your business to understand both sides: clean RTL design and robust DFT implementation. 
 You know that R2G flow development lives or dies based on decisions made during front-end design. A poorly structured hierarchy, an ambiguous clock definition, or a missing constraint at the RTL level can break DFT insertion, formal verification, and timing closure all at once. You have debugged enough of these issues to spot them before they propagate, and you care enough to fix the root cause, not just patch the symptom. 
 At Synopsys, you will work with customers who need someone who can bridge the gap between front-end design intent and back-end DFT reality. What you build, guide, and standardize will determine whether their R2G flows actually work when it matters. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Lead front-end design and DFT methodology development for customer SoC programs, ensuring RTL design decisions support robust DFT insertion and R2G flow execution
 Work directly with front-end design teams to establish DFT-aware coding practices, hierarchy planning, clock architecture, and constraint definitions that enable clean scan insertion and test coverage
 Deploy and support DFT implementation flows including scan insertion, compression, ATPG, and boundary scan across multiple customer programs
 Serve as the technical bridge between front-end design teams and back-end DFT, implementation, and verification teams, translating issues and requirements in both directions
 Debug complex DFT failures that trace back to RTL design decisions, tool interpretation differences, or constraint mismatches, and drive resolution across teams
 Develop and standardize R2G flow methodologies that integrate front-end design quality checks with DFT readiness and back-end implementation requirements
 Support risk mitigation and schedule recovery for programs where front-end and DFT integration issues are blocking progress
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Customer R2G flows execute cleanly because the front-end design was built with DFT requirements baked in from the start, not bolted on later
 DFT insertion and ATPG convergence accelerates across programs because you caught and fixed RTL issues that would have caused failures weeks downstream
 Front-end teams adopt DFT-aware design practices that prevent entire classes of scan, compression, and timing issues from ever appearing
 Cross-functional teams resolve front-end and DFT integration problems faster because you can speak both languages and translate the real issue
 Program schedules stay on track because you identified where the RTL and DFT flow were misaligned and built a methodology fix that worked
 Synopsys R2G flows and best practices improve because you fed real customer pain points back with enough technical depth to drive methodology and product enhancements
 What You'll Need 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience in SoC design
 10+ years of hands-on experience in front-end RTL design, with significant exposure to DFT implementation, scan insertion, ATPG, or test methodology
 Strong understanding of DFT concepts including scan chains, compression, ATPG, boundary scan, and how RTL design decisions impact test coverage and flow execution
 Proven ability to debug complex issues that span front-end design, DFT insertion, and back-end implementation, often involving multiple EDA tools
 Experience developing or deploying R2G flows that integrate front-end design quality, DFT readiness, and back-end implementation requirements
 Ability to work across cross-functional teams and communicate technical issues clearly to both design and DFT engineers
 Experience working directly with customers or internal product development teams in a technical lead or applications engineering capacity is a strong plus
 Who You Are 
 You are the front-end engineer who actually reads the DFT engineer's bug report instead of forwarding it, because you know you can probably fix it faster if you understand what broke
 When a scan insertion fails, you do not just blame the tool, you open the RTL, check the hierarchy, and figure out what the design is doing that the tool cannot handle
 You think about testability while you are writing RTL, not as an afterthought, because you have debugged enough late-stage ATPG failures to know the cost of ignoring it
 You can sit in a room with a front-end design lead and a DFT lead who are talking past each other, and translate the issue into terms both can act on
 You stay calm when a program is stuck between front-end signoff and DFT insertion, because you have been there before and you know how to find the real blocker
 You build methodology fixes, not one-off workarounds, because you want the next program to avoid the problem entirely

 Lead customer migration to new EDA tool versions by validating flows, identifying regressions, ensuring PPA gains carry through to production designs, and building confidence in adoption
 Act as the technical bridge between customers and Synopsys R&D, representing customer needs internally with credibility and representing product capabilities externally with authority
 Proactively identify recurring customer pain points across engagements and develop reusable solutions, scripts, or methodologies that scale beyond a single design or customer and influence product direction
 The Impact You Will Have
 Customers tape out on schedule because the flow you debugged or methodology you built removed the bottleneck that was blocking their critical path to production
 Synopsys wins competitive evaluations because the benchmark results you generated prove measurable PPA advantage on real customer designs at the most advanced nodes
 R&D ships features that matter because the requirements you wrote were specific, grounded in actual design challenges, and tied directly to customer business outcomes
 Advanced node adoption accelerates across your customer base because the migration methodology you validated gives teams confidence to move to the next tool release without risking schedule
 Customer engineering teams adopt new Fusion Compiler capabilities faster because you showed them exactly how machine learning placement or advanced CTS solves their specific timing or congestion problem
 Synopsys product strategy improves because the customer insights you surface reveal gaps or opportunities the product team had not yet identified or prioritized
 Your customers view Synopsys as a strategic partner, not a vendor, because you consistently deliver solutions that work under pressure, on their timeline, and at their scale
 What You'll Need
 10+ years of hands-on ASIC design or application engineering experience, with deep expertise in physical implementation including placement, optimization, CTS, and routing
 Expert-level knowledge of Synopsys backend tools, specifically Fusion Compiler and ICC2, including logical and physical synthesis, timing closure techniques, macro placement, and routing at advanced nodes
 Strong working knowledge of RTL to GDS full flow, with the ability to debug issues anywhere from synthesis through signoff and articulate root cause to both customers and R&D
 Demonstrated experience working directly with customers or cross-functional engineering teams to solve complex technical problems under tight schedules and high stakes
 Deep understanding of advanced node design challenges (5nm and below) and the methodologies required to achieve timing, power, and area targets at scale
 Experience with static timing analysis tools like PrimeTime is a strong plus, as is familiarity with front-end synthesis flows in Design Compiler or Fusion Compiler
 Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
 Who You Are
 You can walk into a customer war room where a design is failing timing by 500ps at 3nm, ask three diagnostic questions, and know where to start looking before anyone finishes answering
 You do not wait for perfect information to act, you work with what you have, isolate variables, and move toward a solution while others are still debating the scope of the problem
 You can translate a dense timing report into a two-sentence explanation of what is broken and what needs to change, and that explanation makes sense to both the customer lead and the R&D architect
 You are comfortable being the customer advocate in a room full of R&D engineers and the product expert in a room full of skeptical customer architects, and you do not lose credibility in either setting
 You know when to escalate and when to solve it yourself, and you have the judgment and experience to tell the difference in real time without second-guessing
 You stay current on what is changing in advanced node design and EDA methodology, not because it is required, but because you are genuinely curious about how the next generation of chips gets built and you want to be part of shaping that
 The Team You'll Be Part Of
 You will join the Application Engineering team in Bengaluru, working closely with Synopsys R&D, product management, and field teams globally to support customers across Asia and beyond. This team sits at the intersection of product development and customer success, and your work will directly shape both what we build and how customers use it.
 Rewards and Benefits
 We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

We Are 
 Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
 You Are 
 You have spent years designing analog circuits that have to perform under real-world conditions, not just pass simulation. High-speed IO is where you live, and you understand that the difference between a PHY that meets spec and one that ships in volume comes down to the choices you make at the transistor level. You know device physics well enough to predict how a circuit will behave in a new process node before the PDK is fully characterized, and you have debugged enough silicon to know that the layout always matters more than people think.
 Working in advanced CMOS, FinFET, or GAA does not intimidate you. You have done it, you know where the models break down, and you know how to work around it. Collaboration across time zones is part of the job, and you are comfortable translating a system-level requirement into a circuit topology that actually works. You care about getting the design right, not just done, and you have the technical depth to back that up when tradeoffs get hard.
 At Synopsys, you will work on memory interface PHYs that ship in the most advanced SoCs in the world. The problems are hard, the technology is real, and what you design will matter.
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Design and develop high-speed IO circuits for next-generation memory interface PHY IPs including DDR, HBM, and UCIe in advanced CMOS, FinFET, and GAA process nodes
 Execute circuit design tasks from architecture through layout, simulation, and verification with a focus on performance, power, and area optimization
 Analyze and solve complex analog design challenges in advanced technology nodes where device behavior and parasitics significantly impact circuit performance
 Collaborate with global cross-functional teams including digital design, verification, layout, and product engineering to deliver integrated PHY solutions
 Apply ESD and reliability principles to ensure robust circuit design that meets product quality and long-term performance requirements
 Work within JEDEC specifications and memory interface standards to ensure compliance and interoperability across customer platforms
 Support silicon bring-up, characterization, and debug activities to validate design performance and drive continuous improvement
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Enable customers to integrate cutting-edge memory interfaces into their SoCs, directly affecting performance and power efficiency of next-generation AI, compute, and mobile products
 Contribute to Synopsys Silicon IP portfolio that powers the world's most advanced semiconductor designs across multiple market segments
 Deliver PHY IP blocks that reduce customer time-to-market and de-risk their product development in the most challenging process nodes
 Influence the architecture and design methodology for future generations of high-speed memory interfaces used globally
 Help establish design best practices and circuit techniques that will be reused across multiple product lines and technology nodes
 Drive quality and performance standards that define what competitive memory PHY IP looks like in the market
 Support the success of customer tape-outs by delivering IP that works the first time and scales across process variants
 What You'll Need 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field
 5 to 10 years of hands-on analog circuit design experience with demonstrated expertise in high-speed IO design
 Deep understanding of analog design fundamentals including device physics, transistor-level design, and circuit analysis
 Proven experience designing circuits in advanced technology nodes such as CMOS, FinFET, or GAA processes
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to debug complex analog and mixed-signal issues
 Knowledge of ESD protection schemes and reliability considerations in analog circuit design
 Experience with JEDEC memory interface standards (DDR, HBM, LPDDR) or familiarity with signal integrity and power integrity concepts is a plus
 Who You Are 
 You can take a system-level timing budget and translate it into a circuit topology that meets it without over-designing or leaving margin on the table
 You know when to trust the simulator and when to build margin into your design because you have seen what happens when corner cases show up in silicon
 You are comfortable presenting a design review to a room of architects and layout engineers, defending your choices, and incorporating feedback that makes the design better
 You stay organized across multiple design tasks, keep documentation current, and do not let details slip even when schedules get tight
 You ask the right questions early, especially when requirements are ambiguous or when a spec does not account for real-world constraints
 You work well with people in different roles and time zones, and you know how to escalate issues before they become blockers
 The Team You'll Be Part Of 
 You will join the Silicon IP business unit, specifically the team developing next-generation memory interface PHY IPs including DDR, HBM, and UCIe. This is a global team working on some of the most advanced and high-performance IP blocks in the Synopsys portfolio, collaborating across design, verification, and product engineering functions to deliver solutions that ship in cutting-edge SoCs worldwide.
 Rewards and Benefits 
 We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

Back to jobs Electrical Engineer (f/m/x)
 Munich Apply Who we are 
 Founded in 2019, Marvel Fusion is Europe’s leading fusion energy company, uniting 120 scientists, engineers, and entrepreneurs across our locations in Munich and Colorado .   
 Backed by over €385 million in public and private funding, we’re driven by a shared mission: to deliver clean, abundant energy to the world.   
 Why Marvel Fusion 
 By joining us, you will be:
 Solving one of the most complex technological challenges known to humanity, harnessing Fusion on Earth
 Part of a highly purpose-driven team working on providing the world with clean, safe and abundant energy
 Working alongside world-leading scientists and entrepreneurs in the field of Fusion
 Part of a start-up where growth on a company and individual level is the default
 Deine Wirkung
 In dieser vielseitigen Rolle bist du die zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Engineering und Experimentalphysik. Du übersetzt komplexe Anforderungen in robuste elektrische Lösungen. Gemeinsam mit einem interdisziplinären Engineering-Team konzipierst, baust und validierst du hochwertige Versuchsaufbauten mit anspruchsvollen elektromechanischen Systemen. Deine Arbeit trägt direkt zum Erfolg unserer Experimentkampagnen bei: Du sorgst für sichere, zuverlässige und sauber strukturierte elektrische Systeme in einem  Hochspannungsumfeld . Mit etablierten Best Practices und Normen ermöglichst du Spitzenforschung auf höchstem Sicherheits- und Technikniveau.
 Deine Aufgaben
 Konstruktion und Dokumentation elektrischer Systeme in EPLAN Electric P8 und EPLAN Cable Pro D, inkl. Stromlaufplänen, Klemmenplänen, Makros und Kabellisten
 Konzeption, Aufbau und Verdrahtung von Schaltschränken, Gehäusen und PDUs für Nieder- und Hochspannungsanwendungen
 Festlegung und Umsetzung fachgerechter Kabelführung, Schirmung, Kennzeichnung und Montage
 Auswahl und Integration von Relais, Fehlerstromschutzschaltern (RCD/RCBO), Schützen, Leistungsschaltern und weiteren Schutzeinrichtungen
 Durchführung elektrischer Gefährdungsbeurteilungen und Festlegung von Schutzmaßnahmen für Schaltschränke und Anlagen
 Übernahme der Rolle als Verantwortliche Elektrofachkraft (VEFK) für Anlagen in deinem Zuständigkeitsbereich – falls du die Qualifikation noch nicht hast, nach Abschluss der von uns finanzierten VEFK-Weiterbildung
 Unterstützung bei Inbetriebnahme, Prüfung und Fehlersuche, intern und bei Experimentkampagnen vor Ort
 Mitwirkung an Design-Reviews zu Schaltschranklayout, Schutzkonzepten, Erdung und EMV
 Pflege einer strukturierten Dokumentation inkl. Schaltplänen, Stücklisten und Konformitätsnachweisen
 Erstellung von Projektzeitplänen, Budgetverfolgung und Koordination der Beschaffung für Schaltschrank- und Gehäuseaufbauten
 Organisation paralleler Projekte: Fortschritt, offene Aufgaben und Prioritäten behältst du stets im Blick
 Was du mitbringst
 Abgeschlossenes Studium der Elektrotechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung oder eine Qualifikation als Meister:in bzw. Techniker:in mit entsprechender Berufserfahrung
 Mindestens 3 Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung
 Fundierte Praxiserfahrung mit EPLAN Electric P8 und EPLAN Cable Pro D
 Erfahrung in Aufbau, Verdrahtung und Inbetriebnahme von Schaltschränken, Gehäusen und PDUs für Nieder- und Hochspannungsanwendungen
 Sicherer Umgang mit Kabelführung, Crimpen, Schirmung und professionellen Montagetechniken
 Du kannst elektrische Zeichnungen, Stromlaufpläne und Verdrahtungspläne lesen, interpretieren und erstellen
 Gute Kenntnisse von Relais, RCDs/RCBOs, Schützen, Leistungsschaltern und Sicherheitseinrichtungen
 Erfahrung in der Erstellung elektrischer Gefährdungsbeurteilungen
 Kenntnis deutscher und europäischer Normen und Vorschriften wie DIN VDE 0100, DIN EN 61439, DIN EN 60204-1 und DGUV Vorschrift 3
 VEFK-Qualifikation – oder die fachlichen Voraussetzungen und die Bereitschaft, sie zu erwerben. Eine fehlende VEFK-Zertifizierung ist kein Ausschlusskriterium: Wir bieten dir die Möglichkeit einer von Marvel Fusion finanzierten Weiterbildung inkl. Zertifizierung.
 Gute organisatorische und planerische Fähigkeiten, inkl. Budgetverfolgung und Koordination mehrerer Projekte
 Gute Englischkenntnisse und Reisebereitschaft für Experimentkampagnen vor Ort
 Wünschenswert
 Kenntnisse von Normen für Leiterplatten wie IEC 61191-1
 Erfahrung mit mechanischer Bearbeitung, 3D-Druck oder Laserschneiden

Back to jobs New Mechanical Engineer – Diagnostics
 Munich Apply Who we are 
 Founded in 2019, Marvel Fusion is Europe’s leading fusion energy company, uniting 120 scientists, engineers, and entrepreneurs across our locations in Munich and Colorado .   
 Backed by over €385 million in public and private funding, we’re driven by a shared mission: to deliver clean, abundant energy to the world.   
 Why Marvel Fusion 
 By joining us, you will be:
 Solving one of the most complex technological challenges known to humanity, harnessing Fusion on Earth
 Part of a highly purpose-driven team working on providing the world with clean, safe and abundant energy
 Working alongside world-leading scientists and entrepreneurs in the field of Fusion
 Part of a start-up where growth on a company and individual level is the default
 The impact you will make
 As Mechanical Engineer – Diagnostics, you will develop precision mechanical systems and devices used in advanced laser and fusion experiments, from initial concept through installation and commissioning.
 You will translate scientific and diagnostic requirements into manufacturable, reliable designs and take hands-on ownership of drawings, supplier follow-up, assembly, alignment, testing, and troubleshooting.
 Your responsibilities
 Design and develop precision mechanical components, assemblies, fixtures, and positioning systems for optical and experimental diagnostics.
 Create and maintain 3D CAD models, detailed manufacturing drawings, assembly drawings, bills of materials, and technical documentation, including GD&T and tolerance analyses.
 Select suitable materials, components, fabrication processes, and suppliers with attention to precision, cleanliness, vacuum compatibility, thermal stability, and vibration where required.
 Coordinate manufacturing and procurement, review supplier drawings and quotations, resolve fabrication issues, and inspect delivered components against specifications.
 Plan and perform mechanical assembly, alignment, integration, and functional testing of diagnostic equipment in laboratories and experimental facilities.
 Support on-site installation, commissioning, troubleshooting, and design improvements in close cooperation with scientists, electrical engineers, and controls teams.
 Maintain configuration control, design revisions, verification records, and clear technical handover documentation.
 What you bring
 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Precision Engineering, or a related discipline.
 Practical experience designing and delivering precision mechanical devices, instruments, or optomechanical assemblies.
 Proficiency in 3D CAD and production drawings (preferably Autodesk Inventor or SolidWorks), including GD&T, tolerance stack-ups, and design for manufacturing and assembly.
 Understanding of machining, fabrication, materials, fasteners, bearings, alignment methods, and metrology.
 Hands-on experience supporting manufacturing, mechanical assembly, testing, installation, or commissioning.
 Ability to communicate technical requirements and coordinate effectively with suppliers and multidisciplinary teams.
 What sets you apart
 Experience with scientific diagnostics, optical instruments, laser facilities, beamlines, or experimental physics equipment.
 Experience designing for high vacuum, cleanrooms, low vibration, thermal stability, or micron-level positioning and alignment.
 Knowledge of precision motion stages, actuators, kinematic mounts, and measurement instruments.
 Experience with finite-element analysis, prototype validation, acceptance testing, and commissioning at external facilities.
 A practical, detail-oriented approach with ownership from design through operational handover.
 What we offer
 Our mission is motivation enough for many. But we also support our team with benefits that foster wellbeing and growth:
 Public Transport Subsidy
 Employee Incentive Program
 Phone Bill Reimbursement
 Wellpass or Complimentary Private Health Insurance
 Professional Learning & Development Budget
 Relocation Support
 Company Pension Plan
 30 Days of Vacation plus additional half day on 24. & 31.Dec.
 Modern Office in the center of Munich
 Healthy office snacks
 Regular Team Events

Back to jobs New R&D Mechanical Engineer
 Munich Apply Who we are 
 Founded in 2019, Marvel Fusion is Europe’s leading fusion energy company, uniting 120 scientists, engineers, and entrepreneurs across our locations in Munich and Colorado .   
 Backed by over €385 million in public and private funding, we’re driven by a shared mission: to deliver clean, abundant energy to the world.   
 Why Marvel Fusion 
 By joining us, you will be:
 Solving one of the most complex technological challenges known to humanity, harnessing Fusion on Earth
 Part of a highly purpose-driven team working on providing the world with clean, safe and abundant energy
 Working alongside world-leading scientists and entrepreneurs in the field of Fusion
 Part of a start-up where growth on a company and individual level is the default
 The impact you will make
 As a Mechanical Engineer – Precision Devices & Manufacturing, you will contribute the mechanical design and realization of high-precision devices, machinery, mechanisms and tooling for advanced laser and fusion technology. Your work will cover the full development cycle: requirements, concept design, detailed engineering, prototyping, manufacturing, inspection, assembly, testing, installation and commissioning.
 You will translate demanding functional and dimensional requirements into robust, repeatable and manufacturable designs. Your core focus will be precision mechanical engineering, with particular value placed on experience developing molds, dies, tooling and other tight-tolerance manufactured devices.
 Your responsibilities
 Design precision mechanical devices, machines, mechanisms, tooling, molds, fixtures, positioning assemblies and alignment equipment, from initial concepts through detailed, production-ready designs.
 Define critical dimensions, datum strategies, fits, tolerance stacks, surface finishes, material choices, stiffness and thermal stability requirements; evaluate mechanical interfaces, assembly sequences, serviceability and production repeatability.
 Produce and release complete engineering packages: 3D CAD models, detailed manufacturing and assembly drawings, GD&T, bills of materials, inspection requirements and technical specifications; conduct design reviews and apply DFM/DFA principles.
 Own the technical manufacturing interface from prototype to finished parts: select suitable processes such as CNC milling and turning, grinding, EDM, precision finishing and heat treatment; work with suppliers on feasibility, quotations, fabrication, first-article inspection and nonconformities.
 Plan and support precision fitting, assembly, adjustment and alignment; verify dimensions and functional performance, resolve build issues, and lead or support installation, acceptance testing, commissioning and technical handover.
 Install, integrate and commission cooling-water circuits for precision machinery and experimental equipment, including piping, hoses, fittings, valves, manifolds and leak/pressure testing.
 What you bring
 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Precision Engineering, Mechatronics, Manufacturing Engineering or a related discipline.
 Demonstrated experience designing precision machinery, manufactured devices, complex mechanisms or tooling, with accountability for producing drawings and delivering functional hardware.
 Deep understanding of precision manufacturing, machining and tooling methods, material behavior, fits, GD&T, surface finishes, tolerance chains and dimensional verification.
 Strong CAD and drawing capability, including manufacturing-ready documentation, BOMs, tolerance analysis and clear technical communication with machinists, toolmakers, metrology teams and suppliers.
 Hands-on experience across the complete hardware development cycle, including prototypes, supplier follow-up, inspection, precision assembly, functional testing and commissioning.
 Practical experience installing cooling circuits and working knowledge of piping systems, fluid components and instrumentation, including flow, pressure and temperature sensors.
 What sets you apart
 Previous experience in mold design and manufacturing, injection molds, forming dies, precision toolmaking or comparable tight-tolerance machinery is strongly preferred.
 Experience with precision positioning mechanisms, custom machines, scientific instrumentation, optomechanical devices or automated precision assemblies.
 Experience specifying and interpreting CMM reports, geometric tolerances, surface roughness measurements, inspection plans and precision assembly or alignment procedures.
 Proven ability to work directly with machine shops and toolmakers, resolve manufacturing deviations, optimize parts for production, and lead build-to-test iterations.
 Strong ownership, practical problem-solving skills and a design-for-manufacture mindset, with the ability to turn complex designs into reliable, accurately manufactured and assembled devices.
 Experience selecting, integrating and troubleshooting fluid sensors, flow meters, pressure transducers, temperature sensors and associated piping hardware in laboratory or industrial cooling systems.
 What we offer
 Our mission is motivation enough for many. But we also support our team with benefits that foster wellbeing and growth:
 Public Transport Subsidy
 Employee Incentive Program
 Phone Bill Reimbursement
 Wellpass or Complimentary Private Health Insurance
 Professional Learning & Development Budget
 Relocation Support
